Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:
Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.
Article Summary: Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.

Article Title: RuPay credit cards for UPI-first users: What to know
Article Text:
With rising use of UPI-linked RuPay cards, credit is no longer restricted to big-ticket purchases but is becoming embedded in everyday finances.

Credit Is No Longer Reserved For Big Purchases

First, credit card usage at small merchants and kirana stores

Second, value-back in the form of rewards or cashback on everyday spends

Third, more efficient cash-flow management with interest-free period

Not Every RuPay Credit Card Is Built The Same

Does it offer good value-back on my everyday UPI spends?

Does it provide additional benefits on categories where I spend the most?

What are the cappings, exclusions and other terms and conditions on the rewards program?

What does it offer beyond UPI?

What are the fees and charges it entails?

Convenience Should Not Come at the Cost of Financial Discipline

Beyond Rewards, It Can Help Build a Stronger Credit Profile

Looking Ahead

(The author, Santosh Agarwal is the CEO of Paisabazaar)

For years, credit cards and UPI served two distinct purposes. Credit cards for many were primarily reserved for big spends like shopping, travel or big-ticket purchases on EMIs, while UPI since its launch fast became India’s preferred payment mode for small everyday spends such as buying groceries at local shops or paying cab fares.However, the introduction of RuPay Credit Cards on UPI has been a game-changer. By enabling RuPay cardholders to link their cards to popular UPI apps and make merchant payments exactly the same way, but through a credit card, formal credit and payments have been brought together seamlessly.This, for a large section, has transformed how consumers perceive, use, and get benefits of credit cards in their everyday lives.With rising use of UPI-linked RuPay cards, credit is no longer restricted to big-ticket purchases but is becoming embedded in everyday finances. For many consumers, especially those who heavily rely on UPI, this works as a natural extension of an existing payment habit.UPI payments via credit cards bring three main benefits –UPI-linked credit cards can be used for making payments at neighbourhood kirana stores, pharmacies, local eateries, and other small merchants just by scanning the QR Code.They are equally useful for everyday online purchases through quick commerce platforms such as Swiggy Instamart, Blinkit and Zepto, where UPI is often the preferred payment mode. This provides consumers with the opportunity to use credit cards even for smaller spends, without having to carry their physical cards everywhere or look for a PoS terminal. More importantly, it integrates credit into everyday spending habits.Each eligible UPI spend will earn value-back, which makes all transactions rewarding. For example, if you spend Rs. 3,500 at a grocery store and your card offers 1.5% cashback on UPI, you will earn Rs. 52.50. This may look like a small amount for a single transaction, but when multiple UPI transactions earn cashback, you save a significant amount. Some cards also provide accelerated earnings on certain categories like groceries, utility bill payments, dining, etc. , further adding to your savings potential.When you make a UPI transaction, the amount gets instantly deducted from your savings account. However, when this transaction goes through a credit card, it is added to your monthly credit card bill instead of being immediately deducted from your bank account. This gives you an interest-free period of up to 50 days, depending on the card’s billing cycle, allowing you to pay at a later date without paying any interest. This can be particularly useful for managing short-term cash flows.Moreover, frequent UPI users often make multiple small transactions every week, which can clutter your account, making it difficult to get a clear picture of monthly expenses. When such UPI payments are made using a RuPay Credit Card, they are consolidated into a single monthly credit card statement. This makes it easier for consumers to track spending across categories and manage their monthly budget more effectively.Today, all leading credit card issuers either offer RuPay variants of their existing credit cards or other UPI-focused RuPay Credit Cards. However, not every RuPay Card provides similar benefits on UPI transactions. In reality, the value proposition varies significantly across issuers and card variants.Some offer accelerated rewards on selected spending categories, while others provide flat cashback. Some offer strong value in the form of milestone benefits or merchant-specific offers, while others are co-branded with popular platforms. It is important for consumers to look beyond headline cashback figures and evaluate the overall proposition.The most rewarding card is not necessarily the one offering the highest cashback; it is the one that aligns best with your spending behaviour.So, here are a few questions that you should ask before applying for a RuPay Credit Card:The answers to these questions will help you shortlist cards that actually match your spending preferences and where you can actually optimize the benefits.The greatest advantage of RuPay Credit Cards on UPI is convenience. Ironically, that convenience can also become the biggest challenge.Since the payment process feels identical to making a regular UPI payment, consumers may become less aware of their spends through the credit card as they do not see deductions from their bank balance instantly like in case of regular UPI spends.Multiple small purchases and spends can add up and lead to an unexpected and sizeable credit card bill. For this reason, financial discipline becomes even more important as credit becomes integrated into everyday payment habits. Hence, once you get the best-suited RuPay credit card, it is advisable to manage it well through the following measures:· Track your spending and credit utilisation: When you start using a RuPay Credit Card on UPI, regularly monitor your transactions and credit utilisation ratio (CUR). Responsible card usage can help build and maintain a strong credit profile.· Set up payment reminders or auto-debit: Setting up reminders or auto-debit instructions can help ensure timely bill payments and avoid late payment charges.· Review your credit card statement regularly: Do not rely only on your UPI transaction history. Reviewing your monthly credit card statement gives a clearer picture of your total spending and helps you identify unnecessary expenses and be mindful of your monthly budget.Most importantly, a credit limit should never be viewed as additional income. It is simply a convenient borrowing facility that works best when repayments are made in full every month.Many RuPay Credit Cards are entry-level and come with easy eligibility and low income requirements, making them a good fit for consumers who are just entering the formal credit ecosystem.Regular usage, timely repayment of the full outstanding amount and maintaining a healthy credit utilisation ratio demonstrate responsible borrowing behaviour. Over time, this contributes to a stronger credit profile, which can improve eligibility for future financial products such as home loans, personal loans or higher credit limits.Several secured credit cards are also available on the RuPay network – combining benefits of guaranteed approval, credit building and savings on everyday spends. For new-to-credit consumers or those with bad credit, secured RuPay Cards can become the first opportunity to build a positive credit history through everyday spending.The integration of RuPay Credit Cards with UPI represents an important shift in India's digital payments landscape. Rather than asking consumers to adopt a new payment habit, it embeds formal credit into one they already use every day. And as more banks introduce RuPay variants of their credit cards, everyday UPI transactions are likely to become an important channel for credit card usage.For UPI-first users, RuPay Credit Cards offer an opportunity to derive greater value from everyday spending without changing the way they pay. At the same time, convenience should not overshadow responsible credit usage. Choosing a card that matches one's spending habits, keeping credit utilisation under control and paying the full outstanding amount every month remain the key to unlocking the true value of RuPay Credit Cards.But if you are a premium credit card user who is looking for a mix of everyday and luxury-use benefits, then high-end credit cards like the Times Black may make sense for you.
Article Summary: With rising use of UPI-linked RuPay cards, credit is no longer restricted to big-ticket purchases but is becoming embedded in everyday finances. Each eligible UPI spend will earn value-back, which makes all transactions rewarding. Some cards provide accelerated earnings on certain categories like groceries, utility bill payments, dining, etc.

Article Title: Google rejigs AI leadership as DeepMind CEO shifts role
Article Text:
The shake-up comes during a pivotal juncture for Google DeepMind: the flagship version of its latest Gemini model remains unreleased

Google parent company Alphabet on Wednesday announced a leadership overhaul of its AI division, with AI chief Demis Hassabis leaving his main managerial role and as several leaders of its Gemini model, including veteran engineer Jeff Dean, left the company to launch a startup called Discovery Loop. The shake-up comes during a pivotal juncture for Google DeepMind: the flagship version of its latest Gemini model remains unreleased despite a planned June launch, sparking investor and industry concerns that Google is falling behind its rivals Anthropic and OpenAI, each of which scooped up a star Google AI staffer this summer.Shares of Alphabet fell 4% after the news. Hassabis, a Nobel Prize recipient, will take the newly created title of Alphabet’s chief scientist and transition from being Google DeepMind CEO to being its chairman, he said in a memo to staff.Koray Kavukcuoglu, the unit’s chief technology officer, will assume day-to-day responsibilities of DeepMind in addition to his parallel role as Alphabet’s chief AI architect.
Article Summary: Google parent company Alphabet on Wednesday announced a leadership overhaul of its AI division, with AI chief Demis Hassabis leaving his main managerial role. Hassabis, a Nobel Prize recipient, will take the newly created title of Alphabet’s chief scientist and transition from being Google DeepMind CEO to being its chairman.

Article Title: Before the knowledge walks out the door
Article Text:
Everyone in Silicon Valley is racing to build machines that replace human expertise.

Ahmer Inam

, a schoolteacher's son from Delhi, is building machines that inherit it.

When Ahmer Inam appeared on Fox & Friends in June, his mother watched the segment without following much of it. Her English is limited. There was her son on the famous curved couch of American morning television, fielding questions about artificial intelligence, and she understood almost none of the words. She wept anyway. Some distances need no translation, and the one between a schoolteacher's household in Delhi and a Manhattan television studio is legible in any language.Had she followed the argument, it might have surprised her less than it surprised the audience. Because what Inam was defending, underneath the vocabulary of frontier AI, is approximately the oldest idea in civilisation — the one his father practised for a living: that knowledge survives only when one generation troubles to hand it to the next.Inam has spent twenty-five years building artificial intelligence — long enough to remember when it meant symbolic logic in the late nineties, and senior enough to have run AI and data for Fortune 500 companies, Nike and Wells Fargo among them, back when "chief AI officer" was still an exotic title. He is not, in other words, a critic sniping from the cheap seats. Which makes the thesis of Cognisee, the research lab he founded and leads, sound almost seditious in today's Silicon Valley: "We're not trying to replace the worker," he says."We're trying to make the worker irreplaceable."The problem he is aiming at usually gets filed under the bland heading of "labour shortage." By one estimate, more than two million skilled-trade jobs in the United States could sit unfilled by 2030 — electricians, welders, machinists, the hands America needs if it is serious about building factories, chip plants and grid capacity again. But Inam's diagnosis is sharper than a headcount. "America does not have a work shortage," he likes to say. "It has an expertise shortage."Consider what actually leaves the building when a master electrician retires at sixty-eight. Not the manual — the manual stays. What leaves is the ear that catches a motor running slightly wrong two weeks before it fails; the instinct that connects a faint vibration to a pattern in old maintenance logs; forty years of judgment that was never written down because it could not be. The philosopher Michael Polanyi had a name for this — tacit knowledge, the things we know but cannot tell — and Cognisee is, at bottom, a bet that the most valuable training data on earth is tacit.The company's method has a fable-like symmetry. Its AI begins as an apprentice: it works alongside experienced people and learns what they notice, what they ask, how they make judgment calls. Then it turns around and becomes a coach, carrying that accumulated judgment to the newcomer. "First it's an apprentice," Inam says. "Then it becomes a coach." Picture a 22-year-old on his first aircraft-maintenance job, hearing a sound he has never heard before, with the distilled instincts of the country's best technicians beside him in real time. "He's not being replaced by a machine," Inam says. "He's being mentored by one."The repository where all this lives is called, a little grandly, a Wisdom Vault — a secure library of hard-won know-how from doctors, nurses, electricians, factory workers, farmers, small-business owners. Grand or not, the name gives away the emotional register Inam is working in. This is not pitched as workforce optimisation. It is pitched as inheritance.He is careful — insistent, actually — about the question that framing invites: who owns it? In Cognisee's design, the expert decides what to preserve, what to share, and with whom; the contributor is recognised and rewarded; the knowledge belongs to the person who earned it, not to the machine that absorbed it. "There is a big difference," Inam says, "between being monitored and being mentored." The company is incorporated as a public benefit corporation, which he describes as a legal commitment to the worker rather than a marketing pledge.That ownership principle is also where his quarrel with the reigning AI paradigm becomes explicit. The frontier labs, Inam argues, got intelligent by swallowing the written internet — and the written internet is now substantially swallowed, which is why the industry's plan increasingly amounts to bigger data centres and more electricity, even as some of the field's own pioneers warn of a wall ahead. His contrarian wager is that the next leap will come not from more compute but from the knowledge that never made it onto the internet in the first place — and that it can be gathered by consent rather than by crawler.For an Indian reader, the resonance is hard to miss. This is a country that has watched its weaves, its remedies and its craft knowledge catalogued, carried off and sold back to it before. It is also a country whose deepest teaching traditions were never textual at all, but moved from person to person — the guru-shishya parampara, the ustad and the shagird. Inam has spoken about Wisdom Vaults for indigenous and medicinal knowledge, with communities retaining ownership of what they contribute. One way to describe Cognisee is as an attempt to give the world's oral inheritances an infrastructure layer — sovereignty included.The idea is attracting converts from unexpected quarters. Cognisee's co-founder, Alex Giannou, spent nearly two decades on Wall Street financing precisely the data centres and power deals behind the AI boom; he crossed over, in Inam's telling, because the right bet and the smart bet turned out to be the same one. Among the company's early backers is a senior Google executive who helped invent federated learning, one of the foundational privacy-preserving techniques of modern machine learning. And last year the XPRIZE Foundation, where Inam serves as a Visionary, recognised his work with its Global Visioneering Award.None of which quite explains the conviction. For that you have to go back to Delhi. Inam grew up in a low-income household, the son of a teacher — a man who spent his working life on the least scalable expertise-transfer technology ever devised: one adult, one room, one generation at a time. The son's journey to America was not gilded; there were stretches, early on, when he could not always afford to eat. It takes a particular kind of person to emerge from that and conclude that a nation's most undervalued asset sits not in its server farms but in the heads of its retiring machinists and nurses."Every generation should start where the last one left off," Inam says. It sounds like a product principle. It is closer to a family creed — the thing his father practised without ever calling it a thesis, the thing his mother recognised on a television screen in a language she does not speak. Some knowledge, it turns out, transfers just fine.
Article Summary: Ahmer Inam, a schoolteacher's son from Delhi, is building machines that inherit it. The problem he is aiming at usually gets filed under the bland heading of "labour shortage" By one estimate, more than two million skilled-trade jobs in the United States could sit unfilled by 2030.

Article Title: Meta, OpenAI, Google and other AI companies are learning from your chats. Here's how to stop it
Article Text:
Google warns Blackstone, Bridgewater, Bain Capital, KKR, TPG, Moody's targeted by hackers

Why Google Gemini, ChatGPT, Meta AI and others ‘reading’ your Chat matters

How to change privacy settings on ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Grok, Meta AI and other AI platforms

ChatGPT (OpenAI)

Open ChatGPT.

Click your profile icon.

Go to Settings.

Open Data Controls.

Turn off Improve the model for everyone (or disable Chat History & Training, depending on the version you're using).

Once disabled, future chats are generally excluded from model training, although OpenAI may still retain conversations for a limited period for abuse monitoring. Existing conversations are not automatically deleted.

Google Gemini

Visit your Google Account.

Open Data & Privacy.

Select Gemini Apps Activity.

Pause activity if you don't want prompts stored for future use.

Also review Web & App Activity, Search History , and Auto-delete settings to limit long-term retention.

Users should remember that even with activity paused, Google may temporarily retain conversations for security and abuse prevention.

Meta AI (Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp)

Open Accounts Center.

Navigate to Privacy.

Review Meta AI settings where available.

Adjust public profile visibility.

Limit who can view public posts and photographs.

Use available objection or opt-out forms for AI training where applicable in your region.

Because Meta's controls vary by geography and product, users should periodically revisit these settings after major app updates.

Claude (Anthropic)

Open Claude.

Go to Settings.

Open Privacy or Data Controls.

Disable participation in model improvement if the option appears for your account.

Business and Team plans typically receive stronger default privacy protections than consumer accounts.

Grok (xAI)

Open X.

Go to Settings and Privacy.

Open Privacy and Safety.

Review AI-related data sharing settings.

Limit personalised data sharing where available.

Avoid posting confidential or sensitive information in Grok conversations. Because X frequently updates its settings menus, users should check these options after major platform updates.

Microsoft Copilot

Open Copilot.

Visit Settings.

Review Privacy and Personalisation options.

If signed into a Microsoft account, review connected account privacy settings through your Microsoft Privacy Dashboard.

Five habits matter more than any setting

Most people worry about what an AI chatbot tells them. Far fewer think about what they are telling the chatbot. Whether it's ChatGPT helping draft emails, Gemini summarising documents, Meta AI answering questions on Instagram , Claude analysing files, or Grok explaining breaking news on X, users routinely paste personal conversations, work documents, financial details and even medical queries into AI systems. In many cases, those interactions may also be used to improve future AI models unless users actively opt out.The good news is that almost every major AI company now offers some level of control over whether your conversations are used for training. The bad news is that these controls are rarely front and centre, differ significantly across platforms, and sometimes apply only to certain products or account types.Privacy experts say users should stop assuming that AI services are private by default. Instead, they should treat AI settings the same way they treat browser privacy settings or app permissions: something worth reviewing every few months.Generative AI companies rely heavily on user interactions to improve their models. Conversations help them identify errors, refine responses, improve safety systems and better understand how people actually use their products.Companies insist that they employ safeguards such as removing personally identifiable information where possible, limiting employee access, and allowing users to opt out in many cases.Enterprise and paid business offerings generally provide stronger privacy guarantees than consumer versions.Still, many people unknowingly share information they would never post publicly — salary negotiations, legal contracts, customer databases, medical histories, source code and family conversations.The simplest rule is one that cybersecurity professionals have repeated for years: never upload anything to an AI assistant that you would not be comfortable storing on someone else's cloud server.OpenAI allows users to stop new conversations from being used to improve its models through the Chat History & Training setting.How to change it:Google's AI products draw heavily from your Google Account settings. Activity is primarily controlled through Gemini Apps Activity, alongside broader account controls such as Web & App Activity.How to change it:Meta increasingly integrates AI across Facebook, Instagram and Messenger. Public posts and interactions may contribute to AI development in some regions, while users can manage several AI-related controls.How to change it:Anthropic offers relatively straightforward data controls and gives many users the option to exclude conversations from model improvement.How to change it:Grok operates inside X, making privacy settings closely tied to the X platform.How to change it:Microsoft says consumer Copilot conversations may be used to improve services, while commercial Microsoft 365 Copilot operates under enterprise privacy commitments.How to change it:Privacy specialists say changing a few settings is only part of the solution. The biggest factor in protecting personal information is still how people use AI services. They advise treating chatbots like any other cloud-based service and thinking carefully before sharing sensitive information. That means never pasting passwords, one-time passwords (OTPs), banking details or other financial credentials into an AI assistant. Users should also avoid uploading confidential workplace documents unless their employer has explicitly approved the use of AI tools. Where possible, names, addresses and other personally identifiable information should be removed before sharing text for summarisation or analysis. Experts also recommend periodically deleting conversation history if it is no longer needed and revisiting privacy settings whenever AI companies introduce major new features or update their data policies, as defaults and controls can change over time.
Article Summary: How to change privacy settings on ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Grok, Meta AI and other AI platforms. Privacy experts say users should stop assuming that AI services are private by default. Instead, they should treat AI settings the same way they treat browser privacy settings or app permissions.

Article Title: Elon Musk shares video of SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket part crashing into Moon, later issues a clarification
Article Text:
Elon Musk

Fake video viral explosion versus real science

South Korean satellite confirms Lunar impact site

What NASA administrator Jared Isaacman said

SpaceX CEO Elon Musk reposted an AI-generated video claiming to show a discarded SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket stage crashing into the Moon’s surface, before clarifying nearly an hour later that the footage was fake. However, despite the lack of live video streams, orbital spacecraft and ground observatories confirmed the impact. The actual collision occurred on August 5 when a 4,000-kilogram second-stage booster slammed into the far side of the Moon at a velocity of roughly 8,700 kilometres per hour.Musk reshared an 11-second synthetic animation created by social media accounts depicting a bright explosion and a 100-foot crater forming on the lunar surface. The clip garnered tens of thousands of likes and thousands of reposts before Musk added a brief follow-up note acknowledging, “This is fake btw”, accompanied by a laughing emoji.Space tracking experts and astrophotographers quickly flagged the video, noting that no real-time optical cameras were positioned to capture a live video feed of the impact.While live video was impossible, space agencies successfully documented the event.The Korea Aerospace Research Institute (KARI) announced that its lunar orbiter, Danuri, conducted eight imaging passes over the target area beginning 30 minutes before the calculated collision time.KARI released before-and-after imagery showing localised terrain darkening, disturbed lunar regolith and ejected material caused by the kinetic impact. The agency noted that its dataset will be paired with follow-up observations from NASA 's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) to analyse structural changes to the lunar crust.Additionally, astronomers at the Institute of Astrophysics of Andalusia (IAA-CSIC) in Spain captured remote observations from an Earth-based observatory, recording a brief plume of ejected material rising along the lunar limb.NASA’s administrator Jared Isaacman noted the agency will use part of the rocket for setting up a base on the moon.“Well, we're going to leverage reusable rockets to build the Moon base. Now, vehicles like Falcon 9, what ULA has, what Blue Origin is building, you know, Rocket Lab, they're helpful for a lot of the initial infrastructure, but then you've got the heavy lift vehicles like what Starship is capable of doing, which is fully reusable, and the new Glenn rocket that's coming. That's what allows you to put lots of mass on the surface of the Moon,” he said, as per Mashable.In another tweet he said: “For those interested in a spent booster impacting the lunar surface, this rare occurrence has decades of history, going back to the Apollo era, when NASA intentionally crashed spent stages into the Moon for science and seismic research. The reality is that meteoroids strike the lunar surface hourly, with impacts comparable to this upper stage occurring roughly every six days.”“The future lunar base will incorporate reusable spacecraft that not only deliver astronauts and payloads but also become part of the infrastructure itself,” he concluded.
Article Summary: SpaceX CEO Elon Musk reposted an AI-generated video claiming to show a discarded SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket stage crashing into the Moon’s surface. Despite the lack of live video streams, orbital spacecraft and ground observatories confirmed the impact. The actual collision occurred on August 5 when a 4,000-kilogram second- stage booster slammed into the far side of the Moon.
